2609.38371.title: TALK-Dem: Benchmarking Embodied Task Planning under Dementia-Associated Communication Patterns
2609.38371.paper_summary: Existing LLM-driven robot task planners rely on a taken-for-granted assumption of an ideal user whose instructions are clear, complete, and task-focused. However, when interacting with real-world users, especially those experiencing cognitive impairments, such as people living with dementia (PLWD), the planners often make mistakes and even pose physical safety risks. We proposed TALK-Dem (Talking Attributes and Linguistic Knowledge in Dementia), the first benchmark for evaluating LLM-driven robot task planning under dementia-associated verbal communication. TALK-Dem contains 4,800 instructions and covers five typical communication patterns, including Referential Imprecision, Object Substitution, Empty Speech, Topic Drift, and Intrusion, at three intensity levels. Experiments across six open-weight LLMs reveal a substantial robustness gap. Across communication patterns, open-weight models exhibited performance drops of up to 22.3 percentage points compared to ideal instructions. This revealed a critical gap and even danger for real-world applications, especially in assistive robotics, where locally deployable models are necessary due to privacy concerns and connectivity constraints. To mitigate this issue, we proposed the Context-Aware Retrieval from Experience (CARE) method, which retrieves relevant previously resolved tasks to provide task-specific interpretation and planning context. CARE generally outperformed standard prompting baselines across the six open-weight models, improving average task success by 18.1 percentage points over the vanilla prompt. These results highlighted the importance of both evaluating communication robustness and developing effective adaptation strategies for locally deployable assistive robots. The TALK-Dem dataset is publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TALK-Dem-A6B3/.
2609.38371.paper_summary_zh: 現有的 LLM 驅動機器人任務規劃者依賴於一個被視為理所當然的假設，即用戶的指示是清晰、完整且專注於任務的。然而，當與現實世界的用戶互動時，特別是那些經歷認知障礙的人，例如生活在癡呆症中的人（PLWD），這些規劃者經常會犯錯誤，甚至可能帶來身體安全風險。我們提出了 TALK-Dem（癡呆症中的談話屬性和語言知識），這是第一個用於評估 LLM 驅動的機器人任務規劃在與癡呆症相關的語言交流下的基準。TALK-Dem 包含 4,800 條指示，涵蓋五種典型的交流模式，包括參考不精確、物件替代、空洞言語、主題漂移和干擾，並分為三個強度級別。在六個開放權重的 LLM 上的實驗顯示出顯著的穩健性差距。在交流模式中，開放權重模型的表現相比理想指示下降了多達 22.3 個百分點。這揭示了一個關鍵的差距，甚至對現實世界的應用造成了危險，特別是在輔助機器人技術中，由於隱私問題和連接限制，需要本地可部署的模型。為了緩解這一問題，我們提出了基於經驗的上下文感知檢索（CARE）方法，該方法檢索相關的先前解決的任務，以提供特定任務的解釋和規劃上下文。CARE 在六個開放權重模型中通常超越了標準提示基準，平均任務成功率比原始提示提高了 18.1 個百分點。這些結果突顯了評估交流穩健性和為本地可部署的輔助機器人開發有效適應策略的重要性。TALK-Dem 數據集可在 https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TALK-Dem-A6B3/ 獲得。
